question: Which gland releases gonadotropin-releasing hormone to trigger the female reproductive cycle?
explanation: Gonadotropin-releasing hormone is synthesized and released by the hypothalamus in the brain to kick off the hormonal cascade. [learn more](GNS311_U1_T10#GNS311_U1_T10_h1)

question: What usually happens when the delicate hormonal balance of the female reproductive system is disrupted?

options.A: Secondary sex characteristics reverse themselves instantly
options.B: Estrogen production permanently stops across all age groups
options.C: The reproductive organs immediately undergo complete atrophy
options.D: It can lead to issues ranging from irregular periods to more serious health concerns

explanation: Think of hormones like a delicate chain reaction! When one part is out of balance, it can throw off the whole cycle, leading to skipped periods or other reproductive challenges. [learn more](GNS311_U1_T10#GNS311_U1_T10_h1)

question: What is the medical term for abnormally heavy or prolonged menstrual bleeding?
explanation: Menorrhagia describes periods that are excessively heavy or last longer than normal, often draining the body's iron stores. [learn more](GNS311_U1_T10#GNS311_U1_T10_h2)

question: A patient with Polycystic Ovary Syndrome (PCOS) is most likely to show which group of signs?

options.A: High male hormone levels, failure to release eggs regularly, and insulin resistance
options.B: Heavy bleeding, low blood pressure, and severe weight loss
options.C: Complete absence of pubic hair and early menopause
options.D: Frequent fever, pelvic pain, and purulent vaginal discharge

explanation: PCOS is a very common hormonal condition. It usually involves high levels of androgens (male hormones), irregular ovulation, and trouble handling insulin properly. [learn more](GNS311_U1_T10#GNS311_U1_T10_h2)

question: What is a cystocele?

options.A: Benign smooth muscle tumors growing inside the myometrium
options.B: Bulging of the bladder into the anterior vaginal wall
options.C: Herniation of the rectum into the posterior vaginal canal
options.D: Downward displacement of the uterus through the cervix

explanation: A cystocele happens when the supportive tissue between a woman's bladder and vaginal wall weakens, allowing the bladder to sag into the vagina. [learn more](GNS311_U1_T10#GNS311_U1_T10_h3)

question: Why do pelvic organ prolapse conditions often lead to problems with urination?

options.A: Estrogen surges cause the bladder to double in physical size
options.B: Infection destroys the smooth muscle tissue of the ureters
options.C: The kidneys stop producing urine due to chronic pelvic pressure
options.D: The shifted position of the organs changes normal urine flow mechanics

explanation: When supportive pelvic structures weaken and sag, organs like the bladder shift out of place. This makes it hard to empty the bladder fully, leading to frequent urges or retention. [learn more](GNS311_U1_T10#GNS311_U1_T10_h3)

question: Which germs are the most common causes of Pelvic Inflammatory Disease (PID)?

options.D: Human papillomavirus and Herpes simplex virus

explanation: PID usually happens when sexually transmitted bacteria travel upward from the vagina and cervix into the uterus and fallopian tubes. Always good to remember for clinicals! [learn more](GNS311_U1_T10#GNS311_U1_T10_h4)

question: A young female patient has lower abdominal pain and cries out in severe pain when the nurse moves her cervix during a pelvic exam. What is the most likely condition?
explanation: That intense pain when moving the cervix is called 'cervical motion tenderness' (or a positive chandelier sign), and it's a classic red flag for PID. [learn more](GNS311_U1_T10#GNS311_U1_T10_h4)

question: Persistent infection with high-risk strains of which common virus is the primary cause of cervical cancer?
explanation: High-risk types of HPV can cause gradual changes in the cells of the cervix. Over time, these changes can turn cancerous if not caught early by a Pap smear. [learn more](GNS311_U1_T10#GNS311_U1_T10_h5)

question: Why is ovarian cancer so often diagnosed at an advanced stage?

options.A: Patients refuse pelvic examinations until pain becomes unbearable
options.B: Early symptoms are vague and easily mistaken for normal tummy trouble or gas
options.C: Tumors spread exclusively through the lymphatic system
options.D: There are no reliable blood tests or imaging studies available

explanation: Ovarian cancer is tricky because early signs like bloating, mild fullness, or tummy ache look just like common digestive issues, so people often ignore them at first. [learn more](GNS311_U1_T10#GNS311_U1_T10_h5)

question: What tool does a doctor use to look closely at abnormal cervical tissue under a special magnifying lens?
explanation: A colposcopy uses a special magnifying scope to take a closer look at the cervix, vagina, and vulva, usually following up on an abnormal Pap smear result. [learn more](GNS311_U1_T10#GNS311_U1_T10_h6)

question: What is the main reason a patient would have a hysterosalpingography (HSG) procedure done?

options.A: To measure circulating levels of follicle-stimulating hormone
options.B: To check if the fallopian tubes are open and examine the inside of the uterus
options.C: To visualize ovarian cysts and measure their exact physical dimensions
options.D: To scrape the endometrial lining for suspected malignant cells

explanation: During an HSG, a special dye is gently put into the uterus while taking X-rays. It helps doctors see if the fallopian tubes are blocked or clear. [learn more](GNS311_U1_T10#GNS311_U1_T10_h6)
